claim_as_stated: Brynjolfsson, Chandar and Chen 'Canaries in the Coal Mine?' (2025): early-career employment in AI-exposed occupations; 2026 follow-ups. Team: 22-25-year-olds in the two most-exposed quintiles ~19% below counterfactual by June 2026, up from 15% at the July 2025 vintage, via reduced hiring.
correct_statement: Stanford Digital Economy Lab, Aug 12, 2026: 'No Widespread Displacement, but the AI Employment Gap for Young Workers Has Widened to 19%'. Employment of 22-25-year-olds in highly AI-exposed occupations is ~19% below the less-exposed trend as of June 2026 (15% at the July 2025 vintage). Their employment in the two most-exposed quintiles fell ~11% Nov 2022-Jun 2026, while the three least-exposed grew ~10%. The adjustment comes mainly through reduced hiring and shows in employment, not base pay. No economy-wide displacement was found, and there is no comparable gap for experienced workers. The revised paper is 'Canaries in the Coal Mine? Six Facts About the Recent Employment Effects of Artificial Intelligence' (Aug 2026 revision), which adds codified vs tacit knowledge. Follow-ups: the ADP Research/Stanford Canaries Dashboard (monthly), the Stanford AI Economic Indicators project, and the Feb 2026 post on interest rates and timing.
source_title: No Widespread Displacement, but the AI Employment Gap for Young Workers Has Widened to 19%
note: Patterns are descriptive, not causal. Gaps shrink with education controls, and estimates exceed national survey benchmarks. The often-quoted 2025 '13% relative decline' figure comes from the Aug 2025 paper version and is superseded; use 15% (Jul 2025 vintage) to 19% (Jun 2026).

claim_as_stated: ILO generative-AI exposure index: latest refinement (2025) and headline (ISCO-08 task-level exposure gradients with expert validation).
correct_statement: ILO Working Paper 140, 'Generative AI and Jobs: A Refined Global Index of Occupational Exposure' (Gmyrek, Berg, Kaminski, Konopczynski, Ladna, Nafradi, Roslaniec, Troszynski), 20 May 2025, with Poland's NASK. source_title: Generative AI and Jobs: A Refined Global Index of Occupational Exposure (ILO Working Paper 140)
note: A companion 'Generative AI and jobs: 2025 update' research brief also exists. Exposure is not impact.
